MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  DECEMBER 10, 2019

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR MITCHELL at 5:30 p.m. and the City Council convened into closed session in the
Conference Room at City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Director of Community Development/Public Works David Wahba
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton

CLOSED SESSION (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER)

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956(d)(2)
  Significant exposure to litigation: one potential case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

B.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956(d)(1)
  Los Angeles Superior Court Case No. 19TRCV00130; Dr. Hendrik Baars, D.D.S. v. SRE
  DCM PV, LLC; City of Rolling Hills Estates

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

  ***

MAYOR MITCHELL adjourned the Closed Session portion of the meeting at 6:00 p.m. and the City
Council took a brief recess during which time an adjourned meeting convened at 6:05 pm for the
purpose of conducting a workshop to discuss the Marloma neighborhood septic to sewer public
works project (see adjourned meeting minutes).

At 7:33 p.m., MAYOR MITCHELL called the regular meeting back to order in open session in the
Council Chamber at City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Alice Min from the Palos Verdes Library District Peninsula Teen Advisory Council led the Pledge
of Allegiance.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
DECEMBER 10, 2019
 ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development/Public Works Director David Wahba
  Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Traffic Engineer Joanne Itagaki
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT “RECYCLING HERO” DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR OF FREE
  RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE.

  On behalf of Waste Management, Sharon Shapiro Fox provided an update on WM’s
  holiday collection schedule and upcoming changes to commercial recycling
  requirements. She also drew names for this quarter’s “Recycling Hero” winners of one
  year of free refuse service.

  RESIDENTIAL WINNER: 4716 ROCKBLUFF DRIVE
  COMMERCIAL WINNER: TKM BUILDING - 715 SILVER SPUR ROAD

B.  PRESENTATION TO OUTGOING MAYOR JUDY MITCHELL

  MAYOR MITCHELL commented that she has enjoyed serving as Mayor for the past year
  and it has been a privilege to work with her with staff, consultants and her City Council
  colleagues.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ recognized MAYOR MITCHELL for her service to the City
  of Rolling Hills Estates and introduced those present to make presentations to her.

  On behalf of Congressman Ted Lieu, Aurelia Friedman thanked MAYOR MITCHELL for
  service to the community and presented her with a certificate of appreciation in
  recognition of her term as Mayor.

  On behalf of Assembly Member Al Muratsuchi, Cody Bridges thanked MAYOR
  MITCHELL for her service to the community and presented her with a certificate of
  appreciation in recognition of her term as Mayor.

  On behalf of the City of Rolling Hills, Council Member Pat Wilson thanked MAYOR
  MITCHELL for her service to the community and expressed appreciation for the positive,

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
DECEMBER 10, 2019
   collaborative relationship the cities share. He presented her with a certificate of
  commendation in recognition of her term as Mayor.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ presented MAYOR MITCHELL with two additional
  certificates of recognition from Senator Ben Allen and Los Angeles County Supervisor
  Janice Hahn and noted their regret for not being able to attend due to conflicting events.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ thanked MAYOR MITCHELL for her service to the City of
  Rolling Hills Estates and the greater area. She reviewed the many accomplishments
  achieved during her term as Mayor while a PowerPoint presentation provided
  photographic highlights of the year. She expressed appreciation to MAYOR MITCHELL
  for her service to the City and presented her with a photo book highlighing her term as
  Mayor.

  MAYOR MITCHELL expressed appreciation for the recognition noting that it truly takes a
  village. MAYOR MITCHELL commented that it has been an honor and pleasure to work
  with staff and her colleagues on the City Council.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN thanked MAYOR MITCHELL for her service to the local
  community and greater area, noting that she is well respected throughout the State.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN echoed COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’S
  sentiments noting that it is an honor serving with her.

CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of
  the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown
  by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on
  separately.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A-N AS
  PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

  APPROVE.

  APPROVE.

  120119 IN THE AMOUNT OF $229,314.57 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
DECEMBER 10, 2019
 CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

  MAYOR MITCHELL nominated, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  VELVETH SCHMITZ TO SERVE AS MAYOR

  The motion was approved by ACCLAMATION.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ shared her background and love for this idyllic community and
  expressed her appreciation for the privilege and honor of being able to serve this
  community.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ nominated, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL

  STEVE ZUCKERMAN TO SERVE AS MAYOR PRO TEM

  The motion was approved by ACCLAMATION.

  ***

  At 8:18 p.m. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting to a brief reception.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ called the meeting back to order at 8:41 p.m.

  ***
PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Martin Gombert, Palos Verdes Peninsula Transit Authority reminded those present and watching
that PV Transit will be offering its New Year’s Eve Dial-a-Ride service again this year and
reservations can be made by calling (310) 544-3710.

Carmelo Sorce, California Water Service Company, provided a construction update on the Palos
Verdes Peninsula Water Reliability project.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

NEW BUSINESS

A.  COMPREHENSIVE ANNUAL FINANCIAL REPORT FOR FISCAL YEAR ENDED JUNE
  30, 2019

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the Comprehensive Annual
  Financial Report (CAFR) for fiscal year ended June 30, 2019.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
DECEMBER 10, 2019
   Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material). He noted that there are a couple of minor typos that will be corrected in the final
  CAFR.

  Brianna Schultz, Auditor Manager, RAMS provided an overview of the audit process
  including management’s responsibilities and the auditor’s responsibilities. She stated that
  RAMS has issued an unmodified opinion finding that the financial statements are fairly
  presented in all material respects; significant accounting policies have been consistently
  applied; estimates are reasonable; and disclosures are properly reflected.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE COMPREHENSIVE
  ANNUAL FINANCIAL REPORT (CAFR) FOR FISCAL YEAR ENDED JUNE 30,
  2019.

  There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

B.  BUDGET IN BRIEF DOCUMENT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2019-20

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the Budget in Brief document for
  fiscal year 2019-20 noting that this document was created to give residents and an overall
  snapshot of the City’s budget.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL commented that she appreciates that the document is a
  precise, concise picture of the City’s finances.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN concurred that the document is very useful and
  inquired about numbers shown in the home value section. He noted that general fund
  revenue vs. general fund expenditures shows expenditures higher than revenues due to
  use of reserves for capital projects and asked if there a way to present it so that it shows
  the City has reserve funds to cover the CIP expenditures.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested including a parenthetical reference to the
  City’s reserve balance to explain the difference.

  COUNCIL MEMBER  MITCHELL  moved,  seconded  by,  COUNCIL  MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE BUDGET IN BRIEF
  DOCUMENT WITH DIRECTION TO STAFF TO INCLUDE A BRIEF
  EXPLANATION REGARDING THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN GENERAL FUND
  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURES.

  There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
DECEMBER 10, 2019
 C.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: MOCCASIN LANE ADDITIONAL
  TRAFFIC CONTROLS

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the following traffic control
  improvements on Moccasin Lane: 1) move the existing crosswalk on Moccasin Lane to
  the north; 2) install a white dashed line on the street for a waiting line for pick-up and
  drop-off; and 3) provide additional signage for both the crosswalk and the waiting line.

  Community Development/Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, Director Wahba explained that the purpose
  of the bulb out was to calm traffic and provide better visibility for motorists and
  pedestrians.

  COUNCIL MEMBER  MITCHELL  moved,  seconded  by,  COUNCIL  MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY
  COMMITTEE’S RECOMMENDATION FOR THE FOLLOWING TRAFFIC
  CONTROL IMPROVEMENTS ON MOCCASIN LANE: 1) MOVE THE EXISTING
  CROSSWALK ON MOCCASIN LANE TO THE NORTH; 2) INSTALL A WHITE
  DASHED LINE ON THE STREET FOR A WAITING LINE FOR PICK-UP AND
  DROP-OFF; AND 3) PROVIDE ADDITIONAL SIGNAGE FOR BOTH THE
  CROSSWALK AND THE WAITING LINE.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

D.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: PORTUGUESE BEND NATIONAL
  HORSE SHOW REQUEST

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve a Memorandum of Understanding
  authorizing improvements to be made to Arenas 3 and 4 at Ernie Howlett Park, paid by
  the Portuguese Bend National Horse Show and waiving event fees for 2019 and 2020
  years.

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN, Superintendent Goldsmith confirmed
  that the work proposed is necessary and should be done prior to the rainy season.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested that work be done and funded using City
  funds rather than in the way that is currently proposed, given that it is a City facility and
  the project would provide a public benefit.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
DECEMBER 10, 2019
   COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL concurred with COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN and
  asked if there are funds available for the project.

  In response, City Manager Grammer commented that there are QUIMBY funds available
  that have not been allocated that could be used for this project this year.

  Discussion ensued concerning the Portuguese Bend National Horse Show’s (PBNHS)
  offer to pay for the work in exchange for waiving their event fees.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN reasserted his position that the City should pay for this
  project because there is a public need for the work to be done.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF clarified
  that is the Equestrian Committee’s recommendation to approve the PBNHS’s request.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE PROPOSED IMPROVEMENTS TO
  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK ARENAS 3 AND 4 AT AN EXPENSE NOT TO EXCEED
